diagnosis_tt.investigations: • Biopsy and histopathological examination: These not only confirm the clinical diagnosis in the early stages of the disease but are also important to assess the stage of OSMF, degree of epithelial dysplasia, and risk of malignant transformation.
diagnosis_tt.treatment: • Abstention from chewing areca nut (also known as betel nut) and tobacco: This is the first and most important step in the treatment of OSMF.  • Medication: Drugs like steroids, hyaluronidase, pentoxifylline, lycopene, curcumin, spirulina, aloe vera, omega3, oxitard, allicin, colchicine have been used.  • Surgical Removal: In severe cases, surgical intervention may be required.  • Nutritional supplements: Supplementing the diet with foods rich in vitamins A, B complex, and C and iron.  • Mouth opening exercises: Ice cream stick, Ballooning, etc.

diagnosis_tt.treatment: • Removal of the Source of Irritation: This could include stopping tobacco or alcohol use, as these are common causes of such lesions.  • Medication: In some cases, medications such as antioxidants may be used.  • Surgical Removal: If the lesion shows early signs of cancer, it may be removed using a scalpel, a laser, or an extremely cold probe that freezes and destroys cancer cells.  • Follow-up Visits: Regular check-ups are important to monitor the area for any changes or recurrences.
